component.name: Apache Baremaps
component.description: Toolkit for creating and managing maps. The security model describes who is trusted: administrators manage the system, configurations, tasks, and data through the CLI or other administrative interfaces; users interact only through limited, controlled interfaces such as the web interface or API.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Baremaps trust model
blueprints.description: Two roles with distinct trust levels: trusted administrators managing the system through the CLI and administrative interfaces, and untrusted users reaching the application only through limited, controlled interfaces (web interface, API).

persona.description: Trusted. Administrates Apache Baremaps, managing the system, configurations, tasks, and data through the CLI or other administrative interfaces. Fully trusted and responsible for the security of the system and application.
Untrusted. Uses Apache Baremaps through limited, controlled interfaces such as the web interface or API.

assumptions.description: Administrators are fully trusted and responsible for the security of the system and application.
Configuration files and data sources are managed exclusively by trusted administrators.

Apache Baremaps relies entirely on trusted administrators to manage files and data; risks such as file path traversal are low because only administrators have access to critical configuration and data inputs.

threats.name: Path traversal via user-provided files
threats.description: User-provided files are not trusted. If a user uploads a file through an HTTP endpoint, Apache Baremaps must systematically sanitize and validate the content to block partial path traversal attacks (for example a zip file with a path traversal vulnerability).

threats.name: Path traversal in administrator-provided files
threats.description: Administrator-provided files are trusted. If an administrator uses a zip file with a path traversal vulnerability, Apache Baremaps does not systematically sanitize the content, as the administrator is expected to ensure the integrity of the files.

controls.name: Systematic sanitization of user-provided files
controls.description: Apache Baremaps must systematically sanitize and validate the content of files uploaded by untrusted users through HTTP endpoints to block partial path traversal attacks.
